exact_statement: The exact aggregate-B tensor, balancing, coding, point-activation and balanced-selector formulas in ERASURE_LEDGER.md hold for all stated finite uniform Boolean signs. Economical activation and balanced selectors of arbitrary seed tensors preserve their B/H limit; systematic nonzero-column coding kills local erasure. For F=f^tensor m times a bent function on 2r fresh bits, D(F)=mD(f), H=mH(f)+2r and I=mI(f)+r; if D(f)>0 and B(F)/H(F)->1 then H(F)/I(F)->2. The actual parity-block bent family of dimension 2t+2r has H=2+2r, B=2r, I=t+r, TC=2t-2 and TV from its coordinate-product marginals equal to 1-2^(2-2t). These formulas do not establish high-ratio near-erasure admission.

exact_statement: Fix epsilon in (0,1) and finite C_epsilon>=0. If every finite uniform Boolean sign f with B(f)>=(1-epsilon)H(f) satisfies H(f)<=C_epsilon I(f), then every finite uniform Boolean sign satisfies H(f)<=max(C_epsilon,2/(epsilon ln2))I(f). Conversely universal FEI(C) gives the near-erasure premise with C_epsilon=C. No restriction closure of the near-erasure class is assumed, and the premise remains open.
